card.name: Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra Dance
card.tagline: A Salatiga dance depicting Mangkunegara I's elite concubine archer regiment.
card.profile: Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra is a classical Javanese dance originating from Salatiga, Central Java, Indonesia. It portrays the historical female warrior regiment of garwa ampil (concubines) who served under Mangkunegara I. The dance integrates classical Surakarta court aesthetics with the energetic movements of the Prajuritan folk martial tradition. It is a flexible performance piece that can be executed by soloists, pairs, or groups, reflecting a blend of historical military discipline and contemporary artistic adaptation.
card.insight: Commemorating the 17 March 1757 Treaty of Salatiga, the dance depicts the Jurit Ampil, an elite military unit of concubines fielded by Prince Mangkunegara I, armed with bows, arrows, and daggers.

card.profile_long:
The Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra dance serves as a historical reenactment of a specific military display from the 18th century. Its name is derived from three Javanese terms: 'jurit', meaning soldier; 'garwa ampil', referring to the concubines of Mangkunegara I; and 'warastra', meaning bow and arrow. The dance is rooted in the events surrounding the Treaty of Salatiga, signed on 17 March 1757. This treaty was a pivotal moment in Javanese history, involving Hamengkubuwana I, Pakubuwana III, and Mangkunegara I. During the event, Mangkunegara I, also known as Raden Mas Said or Pangeran Samber Nyawa, showcased his military strength to establish his legitimacy and authority. One of the most notable units he presented was the Jurit Ampil, a regiment composed entirely of female soldiers drawn from his concubines, who demonstrated their proficiency with weaponry.

As a performance art, the dance is classified as a free-style category, which grants performers the flexibility to present the work as a solo, in pairs, or as a larger group. The choreography is a hybrid form, blending the refined, controlled movements of classical Surakarta-style court dance with the more vigorous, grounded movements found in the Prajuritan folk martial dance tradition. This synthesis allows the dance to maintain a link to the aristocratic history of the Javanese courts while incorporating the kinetic energy of local martial arts. The dance is not a static historical relic; it has evolved to include modern elements, allowing it to adapt to contemporary artistic trends while retaining its core narrative of female military prowess.

The visual presentation of the dance is highly specific, designed to evoke the persona of a warrior. Dancers wear a costume consisting of a short-sleeved blue shirt adorned with gold embellishments, a belt, and a traditional dodot, paired with knee-length trousers. The hair is styled in a small bun and decorated with a golden crown, highlighting the status of the concubines as members of the royal household. The weaponry used in the performance—jemparing (bow and arrow), endhong (quiver), nyenyep (arrow), gendewa (bow), and cundrik (dagger)—is central to the choreography, as the dancers must manipulate these items to simulate the discipline and readiness of the original Jurit Ampil unit. Makeup is applied to further enhance the character's expression, emphasizing a soldier's focus and resolve.

The musical accompaniment is provided by a Javanese gamelan ensemble, specifically utilizing the pelog scale. The instrumentation includes the gender, kendhang, demung, saron, kenong, kempul, and gong. The musical structure is defined by the use of lancaran, srepeg, and palaran compositions, which provide the rhythmic foundation for the dancers' movements. While the dance is rooted in historical events, its ongoing performance by art ambassadors in Salatiga ensures that the tradition remains a living part of the city's cultural identity.

claims.text: Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra is a classical dance originating from Salatiga, Central Java Province, Indonesia.
The dance depicts the female troops of concubines belonging to Mangkunegara I during the Salatiga Treaty.
The treaty involved three major figures showcasing their military strength.
The choreography blends classical Surakarta-style dance with folk martial movements.
The music uses a gamelan ensemble in the pelog scale with specific instruments.
The dancers wear a warrior costume with a golden crown.
